advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that disables a packaged built-in via the overlay and asserts effective_policy_view projects it with enabled:False and reason 'disabled by overlay'.
evidence: editor_contracts.py:233-234 `for cid in snap.disabled_builtins(gate): criteria.append(_policy_projection(snap, gate, cid, enabled=False))`
editor_contracts.py:194 `return "disabled by overlay"` (only reached when enabled is False)
test_editor_effective_policy.py:153 asserts `house["enabled"] is True`; grep for 'disabled' in tests/unit/workflow returns no hit against the effective view

ABSENCE: no test constructs an overlay that DISABLES a packaged built-in and asserts it appears in the view with enabled:False / reason 'disabled by overlay' — a regression that dropped or mislabeled disabled built-ins would pass all current tests
advisory.finding: The effective_policy_view 'disabled built-in' projection branch is untested: no test exercises snap.disabled_builtins(gate) → _policy_projection(..., enabled=False), so the enabled:False path and its reason 'disabled by overlay' (_policy_reason with enabled=False) have zero regression coverage. Every criterion asserted in the tests is enabled:True.
scenarios: An overlay disables a packaged built-in; a regression omits it from the effective view (author no longer sees what was suppressed) or mislabels it enabled:True

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that write_criterion_overlay with an unrecognized gate (and with an absent gate) lands the entry+activate under plan_review and creates no spurious top-level section.
evidence: criterion_preview.py:513-515 `gate = str(routing.get("gate", "plan_review")) ... if gate not in ("plan_review", "code_review"): gate = "plan_review"`

test_editor.py:416 `test_library_create_criterion_routing_still_requires_project_prefix` authors with routing lacking a gate key but only asserts `ok_status == 200` — it does not assert the entry landed under plan_review
ABSENCE: no test supplies gate='<unrecognized>' and asserts data has no unexpected top-level section and the entry+activate landed under plan_review
advisory.finding: The write_criterion_overlay unknown/invalid-gate fallback is untested: `if gate not in ("plan_review", "code_review"): gate = "plan_review"` and the absent-gate default are exercised only implicitly (routing with no gate) without any assertion on the landing section, and no test passes a bogus gate value (e.g. 'billing_review') to confirm it does NOT create a spurious top-level section and instead falls back to plan_review.
scenarios: A malformed/unknown gate string in routing; a regression writes it as a new top-level section (data['billing_review']) instead of clamping to plan_review, producing an overlay the snapshot compiler ignores or rejects
